frames.narration: Midnight passes and the scheduler creates the run for logical date 03-03: four task instances (extract, clean, aggregate, publish), all queued. It dispatches extract, the only task with no upstream.
Extract and clean succeed, each writing its 10 rows to the partition for 03-03. Every state change is written to the metadata database before the next task is released.
Aggregate starts. The worker writes 5 of its 10 rows, then the node is lost. The table now holds a half-written aggregate.

The attempt is marked failed. The retry policy allows 2 retries, so the scheduler waits 2 minutes and starts attempt 2. Because aggregate overwrites its own partition, the 5 stray rows will be replaced, not added to.
The cause is not transient (the source schema changed), so attempts 2 and 3 fail too, after waits of 2 and 4 minutes. Retries are exhausted: aggregate is failed.
Publish never runs. The scheduler marks it upstream_failed and alerts the operator, so no dashboard shows the half table as final. Two days of the other dates are untouched.
The operator fixes the schema mapping, then clears aggregate and everything downstream of it. Only those two instances go back to queued; extract and clean keep their results.

Aggregate re-runs with the logical date 03-03 and replaces its partition with all 10 rows, then publish runs. The table holds exactly 40 rows. An append-style load would have left 5 + 10 = 15 aggregate rows and a wrong total.
